calendar.note: One synthetic calendar day per abstract T-session; not an exchange calendar.

interpretation: Expected E/P/TP/FN values are manually copied from the review table, never generated by scoring.py.
The 21-session stage right context preserves the old fixture maturity T126; production research defaults remain independently tested at 42.
Known masks and event books are hand-given truth worlds, not labels generated from prices.
All forecast rows represent actual notifications, including revisions and duplicate episodes.
Cases are independent worlds; aggregate results are not model accuracy.

cases.title: Inclusive ten-session interval and exact five-session lead
cases.manual_reason: T100 through T109 is ten sessions inclusive; T100-T95 is five.

cases.title: Right endpoint is included
cases.manual_reason: The peak T100 is exactly the right endpoint, not outside a half-open interval.

cases.title: Eleven-session interval fails width
cases.manual_reason: Containment is true but inclusive width is eleven; P remains one.

cases.title: Only four actionable sessions of lead
cases.manual_reason: T100-T96 is four, so event lead and whole-window lead fail.

cases.title: Revision cannot repair wrong first interval
cases.manual_reason: First interval excludes T100; same-scope revision diagnoses a hit without repairing TP.

cases.title: Early computation but late public availability
cases.manual_reason: Only published T95 after close and actionable T96 count; cutoff T89 is not first alert.

cases.title: Scale abstention is not a stage claim
cases.manual_reason: Timing can be diagnosed; no stage assertion exists, so P is zero and stage FN remains one.

cases.title: Short-only peak cannot satisfy stage assertion
cases.manual_reason: A mature short event exists, but the complete stage horizon has no stage event.

cases.title: Short claim does not identify the stage label
cases.manual_reason: The same family has both true labels, but only short scope was asserted.

cases.title: Both scope binds one family
cases.manual_reason: Both labels refer to F100, and one family success cannot be advertised as two.

cases.title: Completed no-signal runs do not remove the event denominator
cases.manual_reason: Six scheduled runs completed with no signal; the known stage event remains a miss.

cases.title: Failed and missed runs do not remove a known event
cases.manual_reason: Prices and labels are known; operational failure cannot turn a known FN into excluded data.

cases.title: Two notified episodes compete for one event
cases.manual_reason: Both independent first claims remain in P; only the first can receive event TP.

cases.title: At T110 neither peak label has matured
cases.manual_reason: Short earliest availability is T115 and stage is T126. Unknown is not absence.

cases.title: At T120 short is known but stage remains unknown
cases.manual_reason: Short=true and stage=unknown must not be converted to a mature short-only family.

cases.title: Expired wrong first alert cannot be repaired retrospectively
cases.manual_reason: As in the source table, this case scores only the original claim. A later future claim needs its own specified target world and is not fabricated here.

cases.title: Complete no-event horizon produces a stage false positive
cases.manual_reason: Known absence over the full horizon and closure is different from an immature or missing horizon.

cases.title: Both stage anchor cannot steal earlier independent short peak
cases.manual_reason: Stage F100 anchors both; short F85 remains missed rather than being silently attached.

cases.title: One family can have different layer representative days
cases.manual_reason: Stage representative T100 passes; short T99 is outside the interval and only four sessions after action.

cases.title: One-session window has width one
cases.manual_reason: Inclusive width is one, not zero; this is a scoring boundary, not certainty.

cases.title: Whole-window lead is stricter than event-only lead
cases.manual_reason: Peak T100 is five sessions ahead, but earliest displayed T99 is only four sessions ahead.

cases.title: Timely stage upgrade starts its own clock
cases.manual_reason: Stage publication is T94, action T95, lead five; it cannot borrow short action T91.

cases.title: Late upgrade cannot borrow earlier short publication
cases.manual_reason: Short succeeds; stage lead is two, yielding a stage failed claim and one stage FN.

cases.title: Wrong first stage window survives a later corrected revision
cases.manual_reason: Stage T92 publication sets the immutable first stage interval. T94 revision adds a notice, not a new first claim.
